title: support_eq_top: the patched module's support is all of Spec R0 via faithfulSMul and smul_lemma
intent: Prove that the support of the patched module M₀ over R₀ is all of Spec R₀ by factoring the argument into two named lemmas — PatchingAlgebra.faithfulSMul (the patching module is faithful over the patching algebra) and smul_lemma (the compatibility of the patching data, which is exactly the map_smul of a quotient equivalence) — and then finishing by a prime-spectrum rewrite that transports the triviality of the annihilator along that equivalence and pulls it back along the surjection f₀.
also_known_as: assemble a support-vanishing theorem from a faithfulness lemma and a smul-compatibility lemma
transport triviality of the annihilator along a quotient equivalence

    (H₀ : ringKrullDim Rₒₒ < ⊤)
    (H : .some (Module.depth Λ Λ) = ringKrullDim Rₒₒ) : Module.support R₀ M₀ = Set.univ

children.name: smul_lemma
children.statement:
lemma smul_lemma
    (HCompat : ∀ i m (r : R i), sM i (Submodule.Quotient.mk (r • m)) =
      sR i (Ideal.Quotient.mk _ r) • sM i (Submodule.Quotient.mk m))
    (m : PatchingAlgebra R F)
      (x : PatchingModule Λ M F ⧸ (𝔫 • ⊤ : Submodule (PatchingAlgebra R F)
      (PatchingModule Λ M F))) :
      PatchingModule.quotientEquivOver Λ M F 𝔫 sM (m • x) =
      ((PatchingAlgebra.quotientToOver Λ R F 𝔫 sR).comp (Ideal.Quotient.mk _)) m •
       PatchingModule.quotientEquivOver Λ M F 𝔫 sM x

applicability.goal_shape: A goal Module.support A M = Set.univ (or, more generally, 'the support of a finite module over a local ring is everything'), where M is a quotient or limit module, a surjection f₀ from the covering ring to the ring A whose spectrum is under consideration exists, and the triviality of M's annihilator is the crux.
applicability.use_when: the module is a limit/quotient whose faithfulness over the covering ring is already available as a named lemma (here faithfulSMul); the action-compatibility needed to build the quotient equivalence is exactly a named lemma (here smul_lemma); and the rest is a standard zero-locus rewrite along that equivalence and a pull-back along a surjective map.
applicability.avoid_when: the faithfulness itself is the hard content rather than a known lemma, so the 'assemble from named lemmas' shape is lost; the compatibility of the two actions does not come from a single named lemma (then map_smul' must be filled inline and one of the two leaf-holes disappears); or the support does not factor through a single quotient equivalence (the computation then needs a different transport).

consequences: The two leaf-holes are real obligations: faithfulSMul must deliver FaithfulSMul (PatchingAlgebra R F) (PatchingModule Λ M F) from only H₀ and the depth equality H, and smul_lemma must deliver the exact map_smul equation so that the quotient equivalence e' is a linear equivalence over the patching algebra. If the compatibility equation in smul_lemma is stated with the wrong scalar (for instance on PatchingModule.constEquiv rather than quotientEquivOver), the map_smul' field of e' will not close, and the whole support computation fails at the structure literal. The remaining obligations are side conditions: the finiteness of M₀ over R₀ (lines 431-432) and the surjectivity of f₀ (line 437-438) are discharged before the transport; the final pull-back needs PrimeSpectrum.comap_injective_of_surjective, which is available because f₀ is surjective. Failure mode: this shape works only when the annihilator of M₀ is exactly the annihilator transported along the equivalence; a module that is not faithful (annihilator non-trivial) would make Module.annihilator_eq_bot.mpr fail and the support would come out as a proper closed subset.
